title: WM-MT145-MergeGovernanceGates
clause: Merge governance: precondition gate (clean source + MT-run state/override), protected-branch consent gate, merge FR lifecycle events + full audit rows

scope.summary:
GOAL: Add the governance layer that wraps the MT-142 headless merge engine with real merge preconditions and a protected-branch consent gate, so a session-branch merge-back only EXECUTES when policy is satisfied, emits merge-lifecycle Flight-Recorder events, and leaves a full audit row (who/what/when/outcome) for every attempt. MT-142 shipped the engine with a `MergePolicyGate { fn check(&self, target: &str) -> Result<(), MergeBlockReason> }` hook whose default is allow-all, and a typed MergeBlockReason::TargetProtectedApprovalRequired arm that nothing yet returns; this MT supplies the REAL gate and the audit/event wiring that the pure engine deliberately omitted.

EXPECTED DIFF SHAPE: New module src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge_policy.rs (registered `pub mod source_control_merge_policy;` in lib.rs) implementing MergePolicyGate over (a) a protected-branch glob policy, (b) an MT-run validation source (the MT-123 cross-family seam), and (c) an approval store; plus a merge audit + FR event emission surface. The MT-142 engine is touched ONLY at its injection point (pass the real gate instead of allow-all) with no algorithm change. Merge-lifecycle FR event KINDS (proposed/approved/executed/conflicted/aborted) are DEFINED by the cross-family MT-161 seam and CONSUMED here: this MT adds NO new FrEventId/SwarmFrEventId strings and re-opens no locked `.GOV/` event manifest; it emits the MT-161 kinds through the existing SwarmEventSink / FlightRecorder EventLedger append path (swarm_orchestration/events.rs). New tests under the handshake_core test tree.

DETAILED SPEC:
1. Types (source_control_merge_policy.rs):
   pub struct ProtectedBranchPolicy { pub protected_globs: Vec<String> }  // e.g. ["main","master","release/*"]; gitignore-style glob match on the TARGET branch name; empty list = nothing protected.
   pub enum MtRunValidationVerdict { Satisfied, Unsatisfied { failing: Vec<String> }, Overridden { operator_id: String, reason: String } }
   pub trait MtRunValidationSource: Send + Sync { fn validation_state(&self, source_branch: &str, session_id: &str) -> Result<MtRunValidationVerdict, SourceControlError>; }  // MT-123 supplies the real impl; a default AlwaysSatisfied impl is provided for callers with no MT-run coupling.
   pub struct MergeApprovalGrant { pub target_branch: String, pub source_branch: String, pub operator_id: String, pub granted_at: DateTime<Utc>, pub approval_receipt_id: String, pub merge_intent_id: String }  // consent record binding an approval to ONE specific target+source+intent; NEVER a blanket approval.
   pub trait MergeApprovalStore: Send + Sync { fn lookup(&self, merge_intent_id: &str) -> Option<MergeApprovalGrant>; }
   pub enum MergeAuditAction { Proposed, Approved, Executed, Conflicted, Aborted, Blocked }
   pub struct MergeAuditRow { pub merge_intent_id: String, pub actor: String, pub action: MergeAuditAction, pub target_branch: String, pub source_branch: String, pub outcome_summary: String, pub approval_receipt_id: Option<String>, pub at: DateTime<Utc> }  // serde-serializable; one row per lifecycle transition.
   pub struct MergeGovernanceGate { protected: ProtectedBranchPolicy, validation: Arc<dyn MtRunValidationSource>, approvals: Arc<dyn MergeApprovalStore>, audit: Arc<dyn MergeAuditSink> }
   pub trait MergeAuditSink: Send + Sync { fn record(&self, row: MergeAuditRow); fn emit_fr(&self, kind: &str, row: &MergeAuditRow); }  // emit_fr stamps the MT-161 FR-EVT kind string into the payload via the existing EventLedger/SwarmEventSink append; NO new kind minted here.
2. Gate behavior — impl MergePolicyGate for MergeGovernanceGate::check(target):
   a. Precondition: source tree clean is already enforced by the MT-142 engine (status --porcelain=v1 -z); this gate additionally requires MtRunValidationSource.validation_state == Satisfied OR Overridden. Unsatisfied => return MergeBlockReason (a new MergeBlockReason::MtRunValidationUnsatisfied { failing } arm ADDED to the MT-142 enum in this MT, or surfaced through the existing DirtySourceTree-adjacent path — prefer a dedicated typed arm). Overridden is allowed but the operator_id+reason are folded into the audit row.
   b. Protected-branch consent: if ProtectedBranchPolicy matches the target, an approval MUST exist in MergeApprovalStore for THIS merge_intent_id, matching target AND source; absent/mismatched => MergeBlockReason::TargetProtectedApprovalRequired { target }. There is NO auto-approve and NO override of the protected gate other than a real operator MergeApprovalGrant (the consent-gate pattern).
3. Lifecycle emission ordering (the engine drives these callbacks; the gate/sink records them): Proposed (before any git command) -> Approved (only when protected + grant found, or NotRequired) -> Executed (on CleanMerged) | Conflicted (on Conflicts) | Aborted (on abort()/Drop) | Blocked (on any Blocked reason). Each transition writes a MergeAuditRow AND emits the matching MT-161 FR kind. A merge that is Blocked emits Proposed+Blocked and NEVER Executed.
4. Audit completeness: every terminal state (Executed/Conflicted/Aborted/Blocked) produces an audit row carrying actor (session/operator id), target, source, outcome, timestamp, and approval_receipt_id when a protected merge was approved. merge_intent_id is minted with Uuid::now_v7() at Proposed time and threads through every row so the full lifecycle of one merge is reconstructable.
5. HARD RULES (operator + red-team): the protected-branch gate is a CONSENT gate — only an explicit operator MergeApprovalGrant unlocks a protected merge; no env flag, no default, no session self-approval. NEVER force-push and NO push at all is introduced here (this layer governs local merge-back only). No auto-resolution (unchanged from MT-142). Git worktree CODE merge stays strictly separate from CRDT document merging.
6. BOUNDARY: this MT is policy + audit + event wiring ONLY; the merge mechanics stay in the MT-142 engine and the conflict UI in MT-143/146. It does not fetch, push, rebase, or touch CRDT state.

STEP-BY-STEP:
1. Read source_control_merge.rs (MT-142: MergePolicyGate trait, MergeBlockReason, MergeOutcome, MergeSession::begin injection point) and swarm_orchestration/events.rs (SwarmFrEventId table lines 33-109 has NO merge-lifecycle kinds today; SwarmEventSink + FlightRecorder EventLedger append path). Read the MT-123 contract for the MT-run validation state shape and the MT-161 contract for the merge FR kind strings.
2. Create source_control_merge_policy.rs with the types above; register in lib.rs.
3. Implement ProtectedBranchPolicy glob matching (reuse the repo's existing glob/gitignore dependency; check Cargo.toml before adding one).
4. Implement MergeGovernanceGate::check with the validation + protected-approval logic and the AlwaysSatisfied/allow default impls for MtRunValidationSource/MergeApprovalStore.
5. Add the MtRunValidationUnsatisfied MergeBlockReason arm (MT-142 enum) and wire the gate into MergeSession::begin (replace the allow-all default at the call site; the engine API is unchanged).
6. Implement MergeAuditSink emission of MergeAuditRow + the MT-161 FR kind strings through the existing EventLedger/SwarmEventSink append.
7. Tests (scratch git repo + injected fakes): protected target with no grant => Blocked{TargetProtectedApprovalRequired}, Proposed+Blocked audit rows, NO merge commit; protected target WITH a matching grant => Executed, audit row carries approval_receipt_id; Mt-run Unsatisfied => Blocked, Overridden => Executed with operator_id+reason in the row; a clean unprotected merge => Proposed+Approved(NotRequired)+Executed rows and the matching FR kinds emitted; a stale grant for a DIFFERENT source/target/intent does NOT unlock the merge.
8. Run proof targets; record measured output.
allowed_paths: src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge.rs (gate injection point + MtRunValidationUnsatisfied MergeBlockReason arm; no merge-algorithm change)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs (emit MT-161 merge FR kinds through the existing sink; NO new FrEventId strings)
forbidden_paths: app/src/** (GUI IPC allowed only on the GUI MT, MT-146)
.GOV/** (the locked FR event manifest is NOT re-opened here; merge kinds come from MT-161)
src/backend/handshake_core/src/kernel/crdt/** (CRDT document merging is a separate domain; do not conflate with git worktree code merge)
acceptance_criteria: ProtectedBranchPolicy, MtRunValidationVerdict, MergeApprovalGrant, MergeAuditRow, MergeGovernanceGate exist as typed, serde-serializable items in src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge_policy.rs.
MergeGovernanceGate implements the MT-142 MergePolicyGate trait and is injected into MergeSession::begin, replacing the allow-all default with no change to the merge algorithm.

Protected-branch consent gate: a merge whose target matches ProtectedBranchPolicy returns MergeBlockReason::TargetProtectedApprovalRequired unless a MergeApprovalStore grant matches this merge_intent_id AND target AND source; a live test proves no approval => no merge commit.

There is no auto-approve and no env/default override of the protected gate; only an explicit operator MergeApprovalGrant unlocks it (consent-gate pattern), proven by a stale/mismatched-grant negative test.
MT-run validation gate: Unsatisfied => Blocked{MtRunValidationUnsatisfied}; Overridden => proceeds with operator_id + reason recorded in the audit row; Satisfied => proceeds.

Every merge attempt writes a full MergeAuditRow set (Proposed plus a terminal Executed/Conflicted/Aborted/Blocked) carrying actor, target, source, outcome, timestamp, and approval_receipt_id when protected; merge_intent_id (Uuid::now_v7) threads every row.

Merge-lifecycle FR events use the MT-161 kind strings emitted through the existing SwarmEventSink/EventLedger append; zero new FrEventId/SwarmFrEventId strings are added and no .GOV manifest is edited.
A Blocked merge emits Proposed+Blocked and never Executed; no git merge command runs before the gate passes.
No push and no force flag of any kind is introduced by this module (grep-provable: zero '--force', 'push', '--force-with-lease' in source_control_merge_policy.rs).
code_surfaces: src/backend/handshake_core/src/source_control_merge_policy.rs (NEW: ProtectedBranchPolicy, MtRunValidationSource, MergeApprovalStore, MergeGovernanceGate, MergeAuditRow, MergeAuditSink)

implementation_notes: The gate is pure policy: it decides allow/block and records audit/events; it must NOT run git commands itself — the MT-142 engine still owns every git invocation, keeping the no-force/no-push grep boundary precise.

MT-161 is the single source of the merge FR kind strings (proposed/approved/executed/conflicted/aborted); import/reference them, never re-declare, so the governance-owned .GOV manifest stays canonical.

MT-123 supplies the real MtRunValidationSource; until it lands in the implementing worktree, the AlwaysSatisfied default keeps the engine compiling and the seam is proven with an injected fake (same pattern MT-142 used for MergePolicyGate).
Approval binding is per merge_intent_id + target + source: a grant is single-use consent for one merge, never a standing permission — this is what makes protected-branch approval a true consent gate.
Overridden MT-run validation is allowed but always audited (operator_id + reason); a silent override is a governance defect.
FLIGHT_RECORDER wiring here is what MT-142/143/144 recorded as DEFERRED: this MT closes those deferrals by emitting the merge lifecycle events for the whole family.

gui_obligation.not_applicable_reason: Backend governance/policy/audit layer; the operator-facing approve/execute/abort surface is MT-146. Merge lifecycle is reconstructable from the MergeAuditRow set + MT-161 FR events (TraceProjection per HBR-VIS-004).

target_entries: Source Control > Merge governance (preconditions: clean source, MT-run validation satisfied or operator override)
Source Control > Protected branches (protected list, per-merge operator approval/consent gate, no auto-approve)
Source Control > Merge audit (who/what/when/outcome rows; merge lifecycle Flight-Recorder events)

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.note: Emit the MT-161 merge-lifecycle FR kinds (proposed/approved/executed/conflicted/aborted) through the existing SwarmEventSink/EventLedger append plus the durable MergeAuditRow set; closes the FR deferrals recorded by MT-142/143/144.

Emit a diagnostic event when a gate check fails unexpectedly (validation source or approval store error, not a normal Blocked) via the open diagnostic-event API if present; else record DEFERRED-with-reason.
Synchronous policy evaluation with no long-lived runtime; liveness capture surviving a crash adds nothing beyond the audit/FR record.

risk_if_missed: The merge engine stays allow-all: agents merge session branches into protected targets (main/release) with no operator consent, unvalidated MT-run work merges silently, and no audit trail exists for who merged what when — MT-146's review flow has no policy to enforce and MT-148 has no gate to prove.

risks: RISK-1: The protected-branch gate is bypassed — a glob that fails to match (e.g. 'main' vs 'refs/heads/main', or a case/normalization mismatch) or a lingering allow-all default lets a session merge into main with no approval.
RISK-2: Approval replay/forgery — a stale or reused MergeApprovalGrant approves a DIFFERENT merge (different source/target/intent), so consent for one merge silently unlocks another.

RISK-3: MT-run validation is read as Satisfied when it is actually Unsatisfied (stale cache or wrong session key), merging unvalidated work; or an Overridden path is taken with no operator_id/reason recorded.
RISK-4: Audit gap — a merge executes (or is aborted) without a complete MergeAuditRow / FR event, so who/what/when/outcome is unrecoverable exactly when a bad merge needs tracing.
RISK-5: The governance layer starts running git itself (or introduces a push) to 'complete' a merge, breaking the MT-142 no-force/no-push grep boundary and the engine/policy separation.
minimum_controls: CTRL-1 (RISK-1): Target name is normalized to the short branch form before matching; a test matrix asserts protected matches for main/master/release/* and non-matches for feature branches, and asserts the injected gate is the real gate (not allow-all) at the begin() call site.

CTRL-2 (RISK-2): MergeApprovalGrant lookup is keyed by merge_intent_id and re-verified against the live target AND source at check time; a negative test proves a grant minted for another intent/source/target does not unlock the merge.

CTRL-3 (RISK-3): validation_state is queried at check time (not cached) with the exact source_branch+session_id; Unsatisfied => Blocked proven live; Overridden path asserts operator_id+reason are non-empty and land in the audit row.

CTRL-4 (RISK-4): Every terminal transition writes an audit row AND emits the FR kind in the same code path; a test asserts the row set is complete and merge_intent_id-consistent for Executed/Conflicted/Aborted/Blocked, and that Blocked never emits Executed.

CTRL-5 (RISK-5): The gate contains zero git command construction; grep proof target asserts no '--force'/'push'/'--force-with-lease' in the module, and all merge git commands remain confined to MT-142's source_control_merge.rs (re-proven live in MT-148).

research_provenance.source: Verified current code: wtc-multi-model-orchestration-v1 src/backend/handshake_core/src/swarm_orchestration/events.rs — SwarmFrEventId table (lines 33-109) carries WORKTREE-CREATED/MOUNTED/RECLAIMED/CLEANUP-FAILED but NO merge-lifecycle kinds; SwarmEventSink + FlightRecorderSwarmSink + DurableSwarmFrBridge give the append path this MT emits through. MT-142 contract defines the MergePolicyGate hook (default allow-all) and the MergeBlockReason::TargetProtectedApprovalRequired arm this MT fills. MT-123 (ML family) is the MT-run validation-state seam; MT-161 (RD family) is the merge FR event-kind seam. Field practice: protected-branch + required-status-checks (GitHub/GitLab branch protection) is the field-standard pre-merge consent gate; single-use per-merge approval mirrors signed merge-request approvals rather than standing write permission.
corrections: Operator/red-team decisions baked in: protected-branch merges require an EXPLICIT per-merge operator approval (consent gate) — no auto-approve, no env override, no session self-approval; never force-push (no push at all in this layer).

No new FR event kinds minted here: merge-lifecycle kinds are owned by the MT-161 cross-family seam and only consumed, keeping the locked .GOV event manifest canonical (events.rs registry note lines 9-20).
Git worktree CODE merge governance is strictly separated from CRDT document merging (kernel/crdt); boundary stated in scope and forbidden_paths.
